common_name: Athens Rose Lantana (Magenta-Bud Yellow-and-Rose Bicolor Lantana)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants after the last frost once soil has warmed, spacing them to fill in as an upright mounding mass by midsummer.

directions: Grow in ordinary, well-drained soil in full sun; this upright, sub-shrubby selection opens magenta buds that mature to a warm blend of yellow and deep rose-pink, giving each cluster a two-tone glow. It handles heat, humidity, and short dry spells with little fuss once its roots are established, and draws steady butterfly and bee traffic through the warm months. In the milder end of its range treat it as a root-hardy perennial and cut the frost-killed top growth back hard in late winter; further north, grow it as a warm-season annual or overwinter cuttings indoors.

common_name: Denholm White Lantana (Compact Sterile Pure White Lantana)

planting.note: Transplant after the last frost into well-drained beds or containers in full sun; space widely enough to let its low mounding habit fill in without crowding neighbors.

directions: Site in average to lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Denholm White is prized among white-flowered lantana selections for its clean, near-pure white clusters that hold their color rather than fading to cream in intense heat. Its dense, low-mounding habit works well massed as a groundcover-style bedding plant or trailing over a wall edge. It shrugs off summer heat, humidity, and drought once rooted in, needing only occasional deadheading of spent clusters to keep flowering steady through the season.

planting.note: Plant after danger of frost has passed in full sun and well-drained soil, giving this vigorous, dense-mounding cultivar ample room to reach its full landscape size.

directions: Grow in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Dallas Red forms a dense, bushy mound whose flower clusters open yellow and orange before deepening to a rich red, so a single plant displays several colors at once. It is a strong hummingbird and butterfly draw through a long summer-to-frost bloom season and tolerates heat, humidity, and drought with minimal care once established. In warm coastal zones it persists as a woody root-hardy perennial; further north it is best grown as a fast-filling annual bedding or container plant.

common_name: Pink Caprice Lantana (Trailing Soft Pink-and-Yellow Lantana)

planting.note: Set plants out after the last frost in a sunny spot with sharp drainage; its vigorous trailing stems benefit from a raised bed, slope, or container where they can spill over an edge.

directions: Grow in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Pink Caprice produces rounded clusters of soft pink and yellow blooms over coarsely textured dark green foliage on a vigorous, mounding-to-trailing plant. It tolerates heat and drought well once rooted in and is a reliable pollinator magnet for bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds through a long warm-season bloom period. Cut back hard in late winter where it persists as a perennial to renew flowering wood for the coming season.

common_name: Bandana Peach Lantana (Compact Mounding Tropical Peach-Orange Lantana)

planting.note: Plant this compact, uniform series selection after the last frost in full sun; its tidy mounded habit suits mixed containers and bedding rows planted on regular spacing.

directions: Grow in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Bandana Peach opens clusters that blend yellow, orange, and pink into a warm tropical wash, all on a compact, self-cleaning, sterile-fruited plant bred for uniform habit in mass plantings. It shrugs off summer heat and holds up well in both ground beds and containers, flowering nonstop from planting until frost without deadheading. Give it occasional deep watering during extended dry spells to keep the display dense.

common_name: Bandana Pink Lantana (Compact Mounding Yellow-to-Soft-Pink Lantana)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in full sun and well-drained soil; the compact, uniform habit is well suited to closely spaced bedding rows or mixed patio containers.

directions: Site in average, well-drained soil in full sun; large flower clusters open bright yellow, shift through peachy tones, and mature to a soft, gentle pink, giving each dome-shaped truss a subtle gradient. This sterile-fruited, self-cleaning series member keeps a tight, even mound all season, resisting the legginess of older seed-grown lantana. It is heat- and drought-tolerant once established and flowers continuously from spring planting through the first hard frost.

common_name: Bandana Red Lantana (Compact Mounding True Red Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; its compact, even mound holds its shape without pinching, making it a low-maintenance choice for uniform bedding displays.

directions: Grow in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Bandana Red carries dense clusters of true red blooms that hold their saturated color rather than fading toward orange, standing out strongly against its dark green foliage. As a sterile, self-cleaning series selection it needs no deadheading to keep producing new flower flushes through the heat of summer. It is highly heat- and drought-tolerant once rooted in and draws steady hummingbird and butterfly activity in beds, borders, and containers alike.

common_name: Bandana White Lantana (Compact Mounding Pure White Lantana)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in full sun and well-drained soil; its clean white bloom color pairs easily with brighter Bandana series colors in mixed plantings.

directions: Grow in ordinary, well-drained soil in full sun; Bandana White forms a neat mound of green foliage topped with clean white flower clusters that brighten plantings without the loud multicolor typical of most lantana. As a sterile series selection it self-cleans and needs no deadheading, flowering continuously from planting through frost. It tolerates heat and drought well once established and performs equally well massed in beds or grown in patio containers.

common_name: Bandana Cherry Sunrise Lantana (Compact Fuchsia-Orange-Yellow Multicolor Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; this vigorous multicolor selection fills out to a fuller mound than most Bandana series colors, so allow a bit of extra room.

directions: Site in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Bandana Cherry Sunrise packs fuchsia, orange, pink, and yellow into every flower cluster for one of the most vividly multicolored looks in the series. It keeps a dense, even mound and flowers nonstop without deadheading thanks to its sterile, self-cleaning breeding. Heat and drought tolerant once established, it performs strongly in both in-ground beds and containers through the full length of a Gulf Coast summer.

common_name: Trailing Lavender Lantana (Cascading Lavender-Purple Groundcover Lantana)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in full sun with sharp drainage; the long trailing stems are ideal for hanging baskets, wall tops, or as a fast-spreading groundcover.

directions: Grow in lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun; Trailing Lavender produces a low mat of aromatic, textured foliage studded with small lavender-purple flower clusters from spring through frost. Its stems root readily where they touch soil, letting a single plant spread widely as a tough, drought-tolerant groundcover or cascade dramatically from a container or retaining wall. Established plants need little more than an occasional trim to keep growth dense and encourage continued bloom.
